svg.title: How an LLM tool call runs
svg.desc: When the LLM asks for a tool, the tool's code in the app, such as MCPToolkit.call() or ApiConnection.execute_query(), checks the permissions and the cache. On a cache miss it resolves the call: it reads the credential from its Smarter Secret, decrypts it, signs the acting user, and builds a ToolCall, such as an MCPToolCall, an ApiToolCall, an HttpToolCall or a WebFetchToolCall, of plain values that travel as JSON. It hands the call to the tool runner, from get_tool_runner(), which finds the executor of the call's kind in TOOL_EXECUTORS: execute_mcp_call for MCP clients, execute_api_call for API plugins, execute_sql_call for SQL plugins, through an SSH tunnel when the connection uses one, execute_extension_call for Extensions, whose third-party code gets its settings, switches and caller as plain values, execute_http_call for the web search apis (Brave, Tavily), the Brave image search, the checks of each image's url and websites' robots.txt, and execute_webfetch_call for the pages the web search plugin reads, with its domain policy and robots.txt checked again on each redirect. The executor reads no database and no Secret: it calls the MCP server, the api, the search api or the website, through safe_http, to public addresses only. It returns a ToolCallResult, with a value, is_error, failure and status_code, and the tool's code in the app sends the signals, stores the result in the cache, and gives it to the LLM. The in-process runner executes the call in the app's process. The remote runner sends it, as JSON, in a Celery task through Redis to the tool worker, smarter-worker-tools, which has no database, no Secret and no cloud credential: it runs the same executor, and returns the result through Redis.
